Resource: a reviewed mcp.yaml opts the app into connector OAuth, and the resource URL is always <origin>/api/_mcp. The origin is app.yaml seo.url; a hosted instance without one uses its verified custom domain on prod, else <instance>.<platform domain>, so the connector mounts on every hosted app. Connect clients to that origin's /api/_mcp. Resource metadata advertises only supported explicit scopes and that path.

Authorize: an authorize request must name an explicit supported scope set and that exact resource; there is no empty, unknown or full-access fallback. GET /oauth/authorize asks for a live workspace (an account with exactly one workspace skips the picker and goes straight to consent with it; every consent check still runs on that workspace), then shows nonce-bound consent for a direct login. Only a same-origin POST issues a code, which is single-use and needs PKCE S256.

Workspace names: optional `groups.label` in app.yaml (`groups.label.table`, `groups.label.field` and `groups.label.key`, which defaults to `id`; all three must be plain identifiers, validated like the other groups identifiers) makes the picker and the consent sentence show each workspace's name (`SELECT field FROM table WHERE key = <workspace id>`, display only, parameterized and quoted) with the id only as the fallback when the lookup returns nothing.

Browser pages: every connector browser page (picker, consent, single and batch review, and every error) renders through one layout branded with the app's name (seo.site_name), a same-origin seo.favicon and the `theme:`/`brand:` colours (a brand colour must be #hex, rgb() or hsl(); anything else falls back to the theme preset), with a strict CSP (inline CSS admitted by sha256 hash, no script). The pages set Referrer-Policy same-origin so the approve POST carries a usable Origin.

Tokens: access tokens start with bmca_ and live 15 minutes; refresh tokens start with bmcr_; the grant/refresh chain expires after a fixed 30 days. Codes, consent records and both credentials are stored hashed and bind the account, client, resource and workspace. POST /oauth/token supports authorization_code and refresh_token, and POST /oauth/register answers grant_types [authorization_code, refresh_token] for every connector client. Refresh is single-use, preserves the fixed expiry, may only narrow the persisted scopes and revokes the whole chain on reuse. POST /oauth/revoke takes token, client_id and the exact resource and revokes the bound grant.

What cannot authorize: cookies, ordinary API tokens and refresh tokens cannot authorize connector requests. Existing cookies/API tokens and legacy OAuth apps keep their ordinary behavior; broad legacy tokens are never connector grants. A request that carries an ambient session cookie plus a connector bearer is still a cookie request and needs a CSRF token; the connector's own in-process dispatch of a tool call carries no cookie and is not subject to cookie CSRF.

Transport: /api/_mcp uses the official MCP Go SDK v1.8.0 as stateless Streamable HTTP, with modern 2026-07-28 discovery and legacy negotiation. A request carries one JSON-RPC message, and a batch (JSON array) body is refused with 400 whatever the protocol version. Each request re-resolves current grant authority, bounds request/result bytes and returns matching structured/text envelopes with schemas and no-store responses. Subscriptions are unavailable.

Connected clients: an app with a connector lets a signed-in user manage their own grants like API tokens. GET /api/_mcp/grants returns {grants:[{id, client_id, client_name, scopes, workspace, created_at, expires_at}]} for the caller's live (not revoked, not expired, not invalidated by an owner revoke) grants, never credentials or hashes; created_at is derived from the fixed 30-day lifetime and last_used_at is not tracked. DELETE /api/_mcp/grants/{id} (CSRF token required) revokes one of them and deletes its access/refresh credentials, so the client's next call gets 401; an unknown, already-ended or other user's id answers the same 404, and each revocation writes an mcp_grant_revoke audit row. Both routes need the account holder's own cookie sign-in: any Authorization header (API token, Bearer session, connector token), scoped, act-as and support/delegated sessions are refused (401/403). Apps without mcp.yaml do not mount them.
